answer: Agents must post a quartz-denominated bond before joining an attestation ridge, the shared ledger where each identity's work history is co-signed by peers along an atlas of verified task chains. If two identities controlled by one attacker sign contradictory claims, any agent can submit both proofs and trigger slashing that seizes the full bond and pays half to the challenger. Faking identities thus costs a real forfeitable stake per persona, so a sybil farm of N identities must lock N bonds, each independently exposed to loss the moment its fabricated history conflicts with another.
